replacements.Álgebra: razonar sobre lo que aún no se: Algebra: reasoning about what is not yet known
replacements.Al-Khwarizmi formalizó que se puede oper: Al-Khwarizmi formalized the idea that an unknown quantity can be operated on as if it were known, rules can be applied, and its value can be obtained. That is an algorithm.
replacements.«Si el doble de cierta cantidad más cinc: “If twice a certain quantity plus five is thirteen, what is that quantity?” Only by guessing or trying values.
replacements.Prueba y error · sin garantías · no gene: Trial and error · no guarantees · not generalizable
replacements.Llamamos <em>x</em> a la cantidad descon: We call the unknown quantity x. We write the relationships. We apply formal rules. The result is an inevitable consequence.
replacements.Reglas formales · garantía de corrección: Formal rules · guaranteed correctness · generalizable to any problem of that form
replacements.La clave del álgebra: tratamos <em>x</em: The key to algebra: we treat x as an object that we can move, divide or multiply, even though we do not yet know its value.
replacements.lo que se hace a un lado debe hacerse al: whatever is done to one side must be done to the other. The equality is preserved.
The unknown quantity is now alone. Applying the rules is enough: no intuition or guessing is required.
replacements.Verificación — la prueba de que el proce: Verification — proof that the process is correct
replacements.Al-Khwarizmi describió procedimientos ge: Al-Khwarizmi described general procedures for solving all one-variable equations. The word algorithm comes from the Latinized form of his name: Algoritmi.
